newsitem.title: CHAD: President's party ahead in Chad assembly poll.
newsitem.headline: President's party ahead in Chad assembly poll.

text.p: Chad President Idriss Deby's ruling party took a comfortable lead in provisional results of the Central African country's January 5 parliamentary elections, state radio said on Thursday.
The results confirmed the deep political divide between Deby's Moslem north, which voted predominantly for the president's supporters, and the largely Christian south where the opposition prevailed.

Of 64 seats of the 125-member future parliament elected in the first round, 40 were won by Deby's Patriotic Salvation Movement. Foreign Minister Saleh Kebzabo's National Union for Development and Renewal was second with eight seats, while the rest went to minor opposition parties.
Sixty-one seats will go to a February 23 second round, the radio said, quoting the National Electoral Commission.
A total of 658 candidates from 49 parties contested the elections wrapping up Chad's transition to democracy after decades of internal strife or war with Libya.
Kebzabo, a former journalist and opposition activist who forged a shotgun alliance with the president, was one of four political party leaders elected on the first ballot.
Deby's party won nearly all the seats in the north in the first round.
The commission put turnout at 48.51 percent.
The results will still have to be approved by the country's appeals court. Chad's first multi-party parliament for nearly 30 years is scheduled to be installed on March 31.
International and national election monitors gave first-round polling a clean bill of health, despite complaints of minor irregularities and organisational problems.
Chad has known coups, civil war or conflict with northern neighbour Libya for much of its life from independence in 1960.
Deby, a former northern guerrilla leader, seized power in a 1990 French-backed coup.
After repeated electoral delays, he won a multi-party presidential election in July in a runoff against southern rival and fellow general Wadal Abdelkader Kamougue.
